subject: react
question: Which function from react-dom/client creates a root to render a React 18+ app into a DOM node?
options: ReactDOM.render
createRoot
mount
hydrate
explanation: createRoot(container).render(<App />) replaces the legacy ReactDOM.render, which was removed in React 19.

subject: react
question: What is the virtual DOM, roughly speaking?
options: An in-memory tree describing the UI that React compares to decide what to update
A browser API that replaces the real DOM
A background thread that paints the page
A CSS engine that computes layout
explanation: React builds a lightweight tree of elements, diffs it with the previous one, and applies only the needed changes to the real DOM.

subject: react
question: Which is usually a poor choice of key when list items can be reordered or inserted?
options: A database id
The array index
A unique slug
A UUID generated when the item was created
explanation: Index keys change when items move, so React can mismatch state and DOM to the wrong items.

subject: react
question: Why does React need a key prop on items rendered from a list?
options: To identify which items were added, removed, or moved between renders
To apply styles to each list item
To sort the list automatically
To make each item keyboard-focusable
explanation: Keys give each item a stable identity so React can match items across renders and preserve the right state.

subject: react
question: Which of these causes a function component to re-render?
options: Only a deep change in its props
A change in its state, a parent re-render, or a change in a context it reads
Only a change to one of its refs
Only a full page reload
explanation: State updates, parent re-renders, and context changes all cause a component to render again.

subject: react
question: What does StrictMode do?
options: Makes the production build faster
Prevents components from using state
Enables extra development-only checks such as double-invoking renders and effects
Enforces TypeScript types at runtime
explanation: StrictMode helps find impure renders and missing cleanups and has no effect in production.

subject: react
question: What is an Error Boundary?
options: A browser API for uncaught promise errors
A hook that wraps fetch calls in try/catch
A Strict Mode warning
A component that catches render errors in its subtree and shows fallback UI
explanation: Error boundaries are class components with getDerivedStateFromError or componentDidCatch; they do not catch errors in event handlers.

subject: react
question: Two components of the same type render at the same position in the tree across renders. What happens to the state?
options: React always resets the state
React keeps the state because it sees the same component at the same position
React copies the state to a new instance
React swaps state with the sibling component
explanation: State is tied to the position in the tree; it persists while the same type renders in the same place.

subject: react
question: Why must a component function be pure during rendering?
options: Pure functions run on the GPU
React may call it more than once or discard its output, so side effects during render cause bugs
Pure components skip reconciliation
It is required for TypeScript support
explanation: React relies on render being free of side effects so it can re-run, interrupt, or skip renders safely.

subject: react
question: A component renders either <input /> or <textarea /> at the same position depending on a flag. What happens to the old element's state when the flag flips?
options: It is destroyed because the element type changed
It is preserved and moved to the new element
It is copied into a ref
It is kept until the next page reload
explanation: When the element type at a position changes, React unmounts the old subtree and mounts a new one.

subject: react
question: A parent conditionally renders <Form key={userId} />. What happens when userId changes?
options: Form keeps its state and just re-renders
Form is unmounted and a fresh instance with reset state is mounted
React throws a duplicate key warning
Only Form's effects re-run
explanation: Changing the key tells React it is a different component instance, which is a common way to reset state.

subject: react
question: What does React do during the commit phase?
options: Calls component functions to compute JSX
Diffs the old and new element trees
Downloads lazy component code
Applies the computed changes to the DOM and then runs effects
explanation: Rendering computes what should change; committing applies those changes to the DOM, after which effects run.

subject: react
question: What does hydrateRoot do compared with createRoot?
options: It attaches React to HTML that was already rendered on the server instead of creating the DOM from scratch
It renders the app twice for consistency checks
It only works with class components
It makes the app render without JavaScript
explanation: Hydration reuses the existing server-rendered DOM and attaches event handlers, and React reports mismatches.

subject: react
question: A component calls setValue(5) when value is already 5. What does React do?
options: Bails out of re-rendering children and effects, since Object.is says nothing changed
Throws a warning about redundant updates
Resets the component's other state
Always re-renders the whole tree
explanation: React skips updates with an identical value, though it may still call the component once before bailing out.

subject: react
question: Why does using Math.random() as a key on each render hurt a list?
options: Every item gets a new identity each render, so all items remount and lose state and focus
Keys must be strings
React sorts items by key
Random keys cause duplicate key errors every time
explanation: Keys must be stable; changing them on every render forces React to destroy and recreate every element.

subject: react
question: Since React 18 with createRoot, what happens when two setState calls occur inside a setTimeout callback?
options: They cause two separate renders
Only the first is applied
They are automatically batched into a single render
They throw an error outside event handlers
explanation: Automatic batching in React 18+ groups updates in timeouts, promises, and native handlers, not just React events.

subject: react
question: What does React use to decide whether to reuse a DOM node when reconciling two children lists that both have keys?
options: Only the array index
The text content of the element
The element type and the key together
The order in which components were imported
explanation: Elements with the same type and key are matched across renders, so they keep their DOM and state even if moved.

subject: react
question: What does flushSync do?
options: Clears all pending state updates
Forces the updates inside its callback to be applied to the DOM synchronously
Batches updates across components
Synchronizes server and client state
explanation: flushSync opts out of batching so the DOM is updated before it returns, for example to scroll to a newly added item.
